# jochwacht-sbom 0.16.0 — CycloneDX 1.7, and a bill that the schema accepts

## CycloneDX 1.7 is selectable

`--cyclonedx 1.7` writes the current specification, released on 21 October
2025 and ratified as ECMA-424, 2nd edition. It is backward compatible with
1.4–1.6, and the document this tool writes differs only in the
`specVersion` string: it uses the fields both versions define the same way.

The default stays **1.6**. That is the minimum BSI TR-03183-2 v2.1.0,
section 4 accepts ("CycloneDX, version 1.6 or higher"), and it is what the
installed base of tooling reads. A default is a promise to everyone who
passes no flag, so it moves on a decision, not on a release.

## Fixed: a license your build file states no longer invalidates the bill

`license.id` in CycloneDX is validated against a closed list of SPDX
identifiers. This tool put whatever a build file stated straight into that
field — so a component carrying `BSD License`, which is exactly what a PyPI
classifier yields, made the **whole document invalid** against the published
schema. Anything a strict reader did with that file, it did under protest.

Measured on 26 October 2026 against the official 1.7 schema with
`cyclonedx-python-lib`: before, a bill with one such component failed
validation; after, it passes.

What changes in your output:

| stated in the build file | written before | written now |
|---|---|---|
| `BSD License` | `license.id` (invalid) | `license.name` |
| `MIT` | `license.id` | `license.id` |
| `mit` | `license.id` (invalid) | `license.id: MIT` |
| `Apache-2.0 OR MIT` | `license.id` (invalid) | `expression` |

Nothing is dropped. Wording that is not an identifier is still carried —
somebody stated it — it is simply put in the field that takes wording. The
SPDX License List 3.28.0 now ships with the package, with its provenance
and a rule for refreshing it; a test holds it against the list the
CycloneDX schemas themselves carry, because an identifier can be correct
per SPDX and still be unknown to the schema.

## Checked against the specification, not only against our own tests

The test suite now validates generated documents with `cyclonedx-python-lib`
— a foreign implementation that ships the published schemas — for 1.6 and
1.7. Our own tests can only confirm what we already believed; the schema is
the only authority on whether a document is valid CycloneDX. Both defects
above had passed every test we had.
